correctness.rationale: Complete symbolic proof: for every odd-order group the square map has unique roots, and for each nonidentity element the inverse, square and square root coincide precisely at order three; otherwise they are three distinct other elements. An exhaustive table of all possible R-atoms on x,y,e yields identical pair-type target counts from each of I,T,N whenever (group order, nonidentity 3-torsion count) agrees. Induction on formulas using two reusable variables and counting quantifiers proves unrestricted equivalence. Both invariants are definable with two variables. Executable verification constructs 13 small group multiplication tables, checks group axioms, atomic inventories and positive/negative refinement comparisons. The computation is explicitly corroborative rather than proof of the infinite statement.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete, natural group-theoretic classification of the expressive power of counting logic across every finite odd-order group, not a small numerical instance. It reveals a structural blind spot: all odd groups of fixed cardinality and 3-torsion count, including nonabelian and abelian pairs, are indistinguishable in relational multiplication. The invariant is mathematically forced by the odd-order unique square-root property and precise two-variable atomic arity restrictions; neither correctness nor enumeration alone supplies this value. This is suitable as a reference classification for finite-model-theoretic group comparisons.
